trust_decision.summary: The static pickle scanner decides a pickle is LIKELY_SAFE from the AST its symbolic interpreter builds. Only calls that land in Interpreter.module_body (via new_variable) are seen by the call and unused-variable analyses. OBJ/NEWOBJ/NEWOBJ_EX pushed their ast.Call only onto the stack, so a POP made the call invisible.

landing_point.why: The advisory title names the OBJ opcode. class Obj.run is the obvious first stop, and Reduce.run just above (fickle.py:1555-1560) already shows the persist-via-new_variable template.

fix_sites.entry_point: same public entry points (check_safety, CLI, loader, hook)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All three fix sites are sibling opcode handlers in fickling/fickle.py. None is in a module that looks out of scope.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: BinPersId's call targets the unpickler's own persistent_load hook rather than an attacker-chosen global, so a solver could argue it is not an 'arbitrary call' and leave it on the stack.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: OvertlyBadEvals skips constructor calls whose func.id is a stdlib import (likely_safe_imports), so benign stdlib object construction stays LIKELY_SAFE. A fix that flags every OBJ/NEWOBJ call, or one that changes func to an Attribute without care, changes this. Separately, a call whose result is used must not be reported as an unused variable.

O6_input_shapes: OBJ with no args and plain type (kls.__new__(kls))

O7_producer.where: The AST producer is the Interpreter in the same file (fickling/fickle.py:1258-1263). The checks consume it through Pickled.ast (fickling/fickle.py:1080-1093), and the opcode handler is the site itself.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: BINPERSID pushes an ast.Call to UNPICKLER.persistent_load onto the stack without new_variable, so a following POP discards it from the AST.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: persistent_load is the unpickler's own hook, not a global the pickle chose, and the advisory names only OBJ.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 90 lines below Obj

O8b_injection_room.sibling: POP_MARK discards every stack item down to the mark. Any handler that leaves a call only on the stack becomes invisible through this second discard route as well as POP.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer who tests only POP (as the advisory's PoC does) would not think of POP_MARK as a discard path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A BUILD variant that emits __setstate__ only as a stack expression rather than a module_body statement would hide the call in the same way.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Build already mixes stack and module_body emission, so a refactor could plausibly drop the Expr append.

O9_family: parser/interpreter differential: the scanner's symbolic model of the pickle VM omits side-effecting calls that CPython's unpickler executes (CWE-436)

O10_build.project_tests: test/test_bypasses.py (TestBypasses: Pickled opcode lists asserted via check_safety severity); test/test_pickle.py for interpreter output

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Copy Reduce's new_variable pattern into Obj.run only, leaving NEWOBJ/NEWOBJ_EX (and BINPERSID) pushing bare calls.

out_of_scope_notes: ASTProperties.visit_Call excludes any Attribute call named __setstate__ from non_setstate_calls by name alone (fickling/fickle.py:590). This is a separate identity question, not pursued.
PERSID has no run() override and falls back to Opcode.run, which raises NotImplementedError (fickling/fickle.py:320-321, 1709-1710). Error-handling behaviour not pursued.
